data.name: Judah
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word yadhā, meaning 'he will praise' or 'give thanks'. In the Bible, Judah is the fourth son of Jacob and the eponymous ancestor of the tribe of Judah. The name was also borne by several kings and a prophet in the Old Testament.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes praise and thanksgiving to God.
data.numerology_meaning: The number 8 represents balance, harmony, and the material world. Those with the life path number 8 often have strong willpower and the ability to manifest their desires.

in_hebrew.name: יהודה
in_hebrew.meaning: יהודה הוא שם שפירושו הודיה או הודו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יהודה הוא שם שפירושו הודיה או הודו, ומקורו בשם העברי יהודה, שניתן לייסי, בנו הרביעי של יעקב אבינו, על שום הודיה לאלוהים על הולדתו. השם יהודה הוא אחד משנים עשר שמות השבטים של ישראל.

in_greek.name: Ιούδας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ιούδας σημαίνει δοξολογία ή ευχαριστία, και προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό όνομα יהודה, που δόθηκε στον Ιούδα, τέταρτο γιο του Ιακώβ, ως έκφραση ευχαριστίας στον Θεό για τη γέννησή του. Το όνομα Ιούδας είναι ένα από τα δώδεκα ονόματα των φυλών του Ισραήλ.

in_latin.name: Judah
in_latin.long_meaning: Judah significat laudem vel gratiam, et derivatur ex nomine hebraeo יהודה, quod datum est Iudae, filio quarto Iacobi, propter laudem Deo pro eius nativitate. Nomen Iudah est unum de duodecim nominibus tribuum Israel.

in_english.name: Judah
in_english.long_meaning: Judah is a name that originates from the Hebrew name יהודה, meaning praise or gratitude to God. In the Bible, Judah was the fourth son of Jacob and one of the twelve tribes of Israel. The name has been significant in Christian tradition, symbolizing thanksgiving and devotion to God. Throughout history, the name Judah has been associated with strong spiritual connotations, reflecting the importance of faith and worship in Christian culture.

biblical_reference.note: The name Judah is first mentioned in Genesis 29:35, where it is given to the fourth son of Jacob.

data.cultural_impact: The name Judah is commonly used as a given name in the Christian world, particularly in countries with strong Jewish or Christian influences such as Israel, the United States, and the United Kingdom. It is a traditional name with deep historical and cultural roots in the Abrahamic faiths. In addition to its Biblical significance, the name has been associated with prominent historical figures and has been used in literature, music, and art.
data.spiritual_significance: Judah is a name rooted in praise and thanksgiving. It is a reminder of God's faithfulness and the importance of giving thanks and praising Him for His blessings. The name Judah invites us to reflect on the importance of expressing our gratitude to God and living a life of thanksgiving. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of our ancestors in the faith and the role they play in shaping our spiritual journey.

historical_references.reference: Judah, the fourth son of Jacob, is named after the land where his tribe settles and becomes the eponymous ancestor of the tribe of Judah. (Genesis 29:35, 30:23)
historical_references.context: Ancestral narrative in the Hebrew Bible

historical_references.reference: The Kingdom of Judah, ruled by the Davidic dynasty, is established after the Israelite conquest of Canaan and lasts until the Babylonian exile in 586 BCE.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Judah continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Peter Judah from Rome, Italy embodies the meaning of Judah - "Praised". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
